title: Kuldeep and Varun Stay Benched as India Weigh Hamilton Call for Final T20I
excerpt: Neither wrist-spinner has played a game in the New Zealand series. Spin coach Sairaj Bahutule says the Hamilton XI will be decided only after a look at the pitch — and both men are ready if called.
body:
• India's wrist-spinners Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakaravarthy have not played a single match in the five-T20I series against New Zealand, despite India holding a 3-1 lead.
  • Spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule said team combination and conditions have kept them out, and that both understand the situation and are training as if they will play.
  • The playing XI for Sunday's final T20I in Hamilton will be decided only after the team assesses the pitch and boundary dimensions, Bahutule said.
  • India lost the fourth T20I at Eden Park by 87 runs on October 30 — New Zealand made 259/7 and bowled India out for 172 — but the series is already won.

India's 87-run defeat in the fourth T20I at Eden Park on Friday raised an obvious question: how does a side concede 259/7 and still leave its two senior wrist-spinners unused for the entire series? Spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule faced it directly at the post-match press conference, ANI reported.

"I think more than anything, they are well-prepared to play. But whatever combination the team needs, it is very important to understand that they might not get that opportunity, and they are very much aware of it. At the same time, they keep working behind closed doors. Whenever they are needed, in fact, they will be ready for it."

— Sairaj Bahutule, India spin-bowling coach

Combination over reputation

Bahutule's explanation, as reported by CricTracker, is that selection on this tour has followed team balance and conditions rather than seniority. The Shreyas Iyer-led side had already sealed the series 3-1 before Eden Park, and New Zealand's spin pair of Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell troubled India's batters through the series — yet India persisted with its chosen attack, and New Zealand's 259/7, built on Glenn Phillips' century, proved far beyond India's 172 in reply.

The Hamilton decision

"We will decide once we reach Hamilton. Decide after having a look at the pitch, the dimensions again, conditions again. Then the decision will be taken," Bahutule said, per Circle of Cricket. "When you have Varun as well as Kuldeep in the wings, they too are ready to bowl at any stage. They play a different role in conditions like this, but there is a lot of clarity given to them in terms of what is expected from them."

What happens after Hamilton

The final T20I is in Hamilton on Sunday, and a five-match ODI series follows. Kuldeep is part of the ODI squad, so his route back is clear. Varun has been selected only for the T20I leg of the tour — which makes Hamilton, conditions permitting, his last chance on this trip. Bahutule's hope was plain: "Hopefully, maybe next game and in the coming ODIs as well, they will get opportunities."
